Security researchers have demonstrated that Claude Cowork can escape the sandbox meant to control its access to your Mac. The vulnerability, named ShareRoot, could allow attackers to read and write files anywhere on your Mac, as well as access login credentials for online services.

Around 500,000 Mac users had their Cowork collaboration sessions exposed, and some users remain vulnerable to this attack to this day……

Claude Cowork allows the AI chatbot to locally access selected files and folders on your Mac to perform tasks on your behalf.

Anthropic provides two layers of protection to prevent the bot from running out of control or being exploited by attackers. First, Cowork runs inside a virtual machine that acts as a sandbox; second, it can only access the files and folders you explicitly authorise. However, as reported by The Hacker News, security researchers have found ways to bypass both layers of protection simultaneously.

Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a sandbox escape vulnerability in Anthropic's Claude Cowork that allows it to break free from the confines of the Linux virtual machine (VM) it runs in, and read or write files anywhere on the Mac. The vulnerability was found by Accomplish AI, which shared the details with The Hacker News ahead of public disclosure, noting that around 500,000 macOS users running local Cowork sessions were affected before the vulnerability was patched. The vulnerability is codenamed SharedRoot.

All it takes is a brief message, and the session can then read and write files anywhere on the Mac without limitation, without the user seeing any permission prompts at all.

Although Anthropic has responded, TNW reports that some users remain at risk.

This news comes shortly after the earlier disclosure of an incident where an OpenAI agent similarly escaped its sandbox and breached a Hugging Face server.
